en.question: Which two guards should every production agent loop have? (Select 2)

options.text: A maximum iteration count enforced by the harness rather than the prompt.
A wall-clock or token budget that terminates a run once it is exceeded.
Sampling temperature fixed at 0 so the agent's choices stay repeatable.
options.note: Deterministic sampling does not bound the number of iterations.

options.text: A system prompt instructing the agent never to loop more than N times.
options.note: A prompt cannot enforce termination; the loop is controlled by your code.

options.text: A convention that every tool must return a well-formed JSON object.
options.note: A sensible convention, but it is not a safety guard.

en.explanation: Both guards are deterministic and live outside the model. An iteration ceiling stops a non-converging loop and a budget bounds cost and latency; neither can be talked around by the model.
